tour.subtitle: A private morning at the Cham temple ruins of My Son with an archaeology-minded guide and car, before the heat and the crowds: the brick towers of a Hindu kingdom in a jungle valley, a performance of Apsara dance, and a return by boat on the Thu Bon river past fishing villages and Kim Bong carpentry village.

highlights: My Son, the religious centre of the Cham kingdom for nine centuries
Brick temple towers in a jungle valley under Cat's Tooth Mountain
The early-morning calm, before the heat and the day groups
A boat trip down the Thu Bon river
Breakfast, lunch, private car and licensed guide
tour.overview:
From the 4th to the 13th century, the Cham kings, who ruled central Vietnam from their ports on the coast, built more than seventy temples in a green valley surrounded by mountains, dedicated to Shiva, the protector of their dynasty. The bricks were laid so precisely that archaeologists still debate how they were bonded. Bombing during the Vietnam War destroyed many of the towers, but the surviving groups, restored with international help, remain the most important Cham site in the world. My Son Sanctuary has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.

This private morning tour reaches My Son at opening time, when mist often lies in the valley and the light is soft, with a licensed guide and a car. You explore the main temple groups, watch a short performance of Apsara dance and return to Hoi An by boat on the Thu Bon river.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 6 hours (morning)
• Start and end: your hotel in Hoi An or Da Nang
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, river boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 3 km on paths

WHAT YOU SEE
• The temple groups B, C and D of My Son.
• The site museum.
• An Apsara dance.
• The Thu Bon river and Kim Bong carpentry village.

WHY THIS WORKS
The site opens at 6:00 and is quiet and cool until about 8:30; we arrive at opening and leave as the groups arrive.

WHO IT SUITS
History and archaeology lovers, photographers and early risers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer an easy afternoon and evening, choose our Hoi An lantern tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about one hour. Unexploded bombs once lay in the area; stay on the marked paths, which are fully cleared. Bring insect repellent.

days.name: My Son Sanctuary at opening time, an Apsara dance, and a boat down the Thu Bon river to Hoi An
days.description:
What to expect: the Cham temples of My Son in the calm of early morning, with a licensed guide, private car, ticket, river boat, breakfast and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at 5:15 and drive inland through the dark countryside, about an hour, to arrive at My Son as it opens at 6:00. An electric shuttle takes you into the valley, ringed by forested hills and the sharp peak of Hon Quap, Cat's Tooth Mountain. As the mist lifts, you walk among the temple groups. The towers, called kalan, were built of fired brick and sandstone, with carved figures of gods, dancers and mythical animals, and lingas – stone symbols of Shiva – at their centre. Your guide explains the Cham kingdom, its Indian-influenced religion and art, and how French archaeologists mapped the site in 1898 before the war destroyed much of it in 1969. You can still see bomb craters around the towers.

You have breakfast in the valley, then visit the small museum by the entrance, which explains the restoration and the mysteries of Cham brick-making. At about 8:30 you watch a short performance of Apsara dance, accompanied by traditional Cham music.

Your driver takes you to the riverbank, where a private boat carries you down the Thu Bon river for about an hour, past fishing nets, sandbanks, water buffaloes and riverside villages. You stop at Kim Bong, a village of carpenters and boat-builders whose ancestors carved the beams of Hoi An's houses, and arrive in Hoi An for lunch. You are back at your hotel at about 12:30, with the afternoon free.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:15 – Pick-up at your hotel.
06:00 – My Son temple groups.
07:30 – Breakfast in the valley and the museum.
08:30 – Apsara dance.
09:15 – Boat down the Thu Bon river.
10:30 – Kim Bong carpentry village.
11:30 – Lunch in Hoi An.
12:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A sunset visit is also possible, but the light and quiet are best in the morning.
• Some temple groups are under restoration and may be closed.
• The boat return can be replaced by the car if you prefer.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, My Son ticket and shuttle, Apsara dance, private river boat, breakfast and lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why such an early start?
faq.answer: My Son opens at 6:00. The first two hours are cool, quiet and often misty; by 9:00 it is hot and busy.

faq.question: Are the tickets and meals included?
faq.answer: Yes: the My Son ticket, shuttle, dance, boat, a breakfast box and lunch.

faq.question: Is My Son like Angkor?
faq.answer: It is much smaller and more ruined, but it is older, deeply atmospheric and very important to the history of South-East Asia. Your guide brings it to life.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who enjoy ruins and boats. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The shuttle reaches the site; paths are mostly flat but unpaved. The boat needs a step down.

faq.question: Is it safe?
faq.answer: Yes. The visitor paths have long been cleared of wartime ordnance; simply stay on the marked paths.

faq.question: Can we return by car instead of boat?
faq.answer: Yes, if you prefer, or if the river is too high after heavy rain.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, comfortable shoes, a hat and insect repellent.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: February to August is drier. From October to December heavy rain can flood the area and change the programme.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
